title: The board-lifecycle night: every record got a disposition, and the dead ends got closed where candidates are born
problem: Both boards carried years-in-hours of accumulated records with no dispositions: 8 release failed, 40 dev failed, review queues holding boundaries, and dismissed issues re-dispatched by any lane with budget because candidates come from open forge issues.
findings: /dismiss proved itself in one round: the previously-undrivable (.failed,.cancelled) transition filed 4 release + 31 dev records, each with a written reason; archive stamps followed single-shot on the next sweeps.
The two-step reject-then-cancel races sibling records: dev #1132-r3 finished twenty minutes after a mistargeted cancel while the state counter matched expectations. Verify by record id.

A dismissal teaches choose nothing: dev dispatched #1131 attempts 12 and 13 within one hour, then hopped to #1132. Closing the issues on the forge with verdict comments dropped the candidate count 23->22->21 and the lane moved to genuinely open work (#1151).

The macosx26.5 SDK stamps were our own bees all along: the agent server launches without DEVELOPER_DIR, so worker shells resolve swiftc to full Xcode - caught live compiling drill1151 with -sdk MacOSX26.5. Fixed at the root (scrubbed env defaults DEVELOPER_DIR to CLT) with build.sh's typecheck probe as second line.

'Auto-accept skipped: unknown' was a hand-maintained mirror of policy guards that never learned the committedSHA condition. The policy now names its own refusal (autoAcceptDisqualification); the mirror is deleted.
gate_administrative proved itself in both lanes (#74 release, #75 dev): a cla-only red names its check and stands down instead of waking a bee into an unwinnable fix.
The #1151 bee is the first to DRIVE ITS DRILL - the proof-by-run its #1131/#1132 predecessors never attempted across 13 attempts each.
fix: /dismiss command; forge closures for #1131 and #1132 with evidence-bearing comments and reopening conditions; DEVELOPER_DIR=CLT default in the scrubbed worker env; autoAcceptDisqualification; consolidated skills.
prevention: Every dismissal of a dead-end issue pairs with a forge closure, or any budgeted lane re-grinds it; verify the candidate count drops on the next choose pass.
After any two-step verdict, verify the target record BY ID and check for a still-running runner before trusting counters.
A zero in a lane's token counts means a stale server process, not a broken pipeline - check the server's start time against the emission commit.
Toolchain policy belongs in the worker env, not in hope: a bee's shell resolves tools exactly like any shell.
corrections_to_earlier_claims: I attributed the SDK stamps to a neighbouring agent for a full day; the culprit was measured to be our own bees within one minute of looking at a live process list.
